steps.content: However, you have only enjoyed a few days of hard-earned peace and quiet in the office, and it was once again shattered by a high-decibel shout.
Ch-chief! Something major has happened!
The office door swings open with a "bang." Dudu puts one hand on the door frame, gasping for breath as she tries to speak. Judging from the sweat streaming down her face, she ran all the way here.
Calm down. Tell me slowly what you want to say.
Dudu gathers her breath to talk, but what she says next comes as a complete surprise...

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: Someone from the Drifter Camp has gotten ahold of intelligence about <color=#fb9259>Parma</color>!
Parma?! But I didn't see anything about it in the intelligence agent's report.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: Pfft, how long has he been there? How can he know as much as I do? To be honest, I only realized it when I was chatting with him today.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: It's my fault for not realizing it before... Anyway, we need to hurry and go as soon as possible! You'll understand when you get there!
You look at Dudu suspiciously. You can't tell if that rare look of seriousness on her face means she's trying to trick you again, or if she's really figured out something important.
But considering that anything related to Parma is no trivial matter, you'd rather be safe than sorry. You immediately assemble a team to go investigate the Drifter Camp.
Following Dudu's instructions, you lead a team of five to an old residential building in the southeast corner of the Drifter Camp.

You squint at the ivy-covered walls, which are mottled from years of wind and rain. You then glance at the senior citizens outside the building, who are chatting and fanning themselves under the shade. Your expression becomes a bit perplexed.

options: Are you sure this is the place?

choices.text: Are you sure this is the place?

steps.content: Dudu nods furiously.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: A hundred and ten percent! I live right next door!
...Okay.
You nod and begin to give instructions to the guards around you.
You hide in the flower bed over there, and you guard the door. The rest of you, come up with me.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: Uhh... Well...
Dudu stammers hesitantly. You assume that she's scared, so you pat her on the shoulder.
It's okay, don't be afraid. Just stay behind me when the time comes.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: Ahhh... Actually... Hey!
Before Dudu can finish her sentence, you start leading the force inside. She has no choice but to stomp her feet and follow you.
You give a look to the guards around you. They aim their guns, kick open the door, and rush inside all in one go.
The moment you break open the door, you get bathed in large swathes of sunlight. Yet the scene before your eyes is totally different from what you had imagined...
Instead of a secret hideout filled with contraband, weapons and black-clad gangsters, it's just a plain old-fashioned home.

The decor is old and plain, but also neat and tidy, as if someone frequently cleans it. The extremely simple layout makes the tiny space feel unusually vast and empty. One can get a sweeping view of the entire home from the door, with absolutely no room to hide.
Your eyes all land on the only living being in the room. Standing alone before the window is...
An old lady?
You and the guards gawk at each other for a while. You then finally turn to Dudu.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: Hehe... Actually, I wanted to tell you just now that there's no need to make such a big commotion...
Dudu scratches her head, grinning widely.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: But you were all serious-faced and dispatching everyone here and there, so I couldn't butt in at all.
You take a deep breath.
So the person who you claim has the important information... is her?

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: Yes!

You carefully observe the old lady, who's gazing out the window with blank eyes. She's old and frail, with a lame foot, and doesn't seem to be in her right mind. Even though a bunch of gun-toting strangers just broke into her house, she shows no reaction whatsoever.
You can't connect this common old lady in front of you with Parma at all.
You can't joke about such important things.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: I'm not joking at all.
She walks over to help the old lady sit down on the bed. You also go over, and watch as Dudu starts to peel an orange from the coffee table.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: Granny, why did you go to the window again? How many times have I told you not to stand that long? Your legs can't handle it.

steps.speaker: Old Lady
steps.content: ...Who is it? You... I don't know you...
The old lady stares blankly at Dudu for a while. Then, a wary look appears on her face. She slurs her words and has trouble speaking, but Dudu understands her effortlessly.
Dudu lets out a helpless sigh. She stuffs half the orange into her mouth, then puts the other half into the old lady's hand.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: Don't you remember me? I'm Dudu. I live next door.

steps.speaker: Old Lady
steps.content: You... Pa... ma... Give me back... Pa... ma...
Frowning, you listen to her mumble the word "Pa... ma" over and over again, but you just can't make out what the syllable in the middle is.
Dudu takes a glance at you, then starts to gently question the old lady.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: You keep saying "Parma, Parma." Who is Parma?

steps.speaker: Old Lady
steps.content: Pa... ma... important...

steps.speaker: Old Lady
steps.content: The old elm tree... climb the tree...

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: ...What?

steps.speaker: Old Lady
steps.content: In the chicken coop...

steps.speaker: Old Lady
steps.content: I still... wait...
Totally befuddled, you cast a puzzled look at Dudu. The old lady suddenly becomes agitated for no reason. Stomping her cane with all her might, she starts to shoo you away.

steps.speaker: Old Lady
steps.content: Get out! You're not welcome here! Leave! Leave!

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: How come you... You're so full of energy. It doesn't seem like anything bad happened... Sigh, okay okay, we're leaving! Quit stomping your cane!
After shooing all of you to the door, she hobbles back to the window, leaving you to face her frail, stooped but stubborn back.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: I really don't know what there is to look all day...
What did she mean by "elm tree" and "chicken coop?"

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: Who knows? She has some mental problems and can't speak clearly. It seems to be caused by a tumor in her head. She was already like this before I moved here. The last time she was clear-headed was two or three months ago, when she asked me to arrange her funeral after she dies.
Dudu scratches her head, then looks at you as if seeking praise.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: You heard her, didn't you? I wasn't lying. She really knows about Parma.
But was she really saying "Parma"? I could only make out "pa" at the beginning and "ma" at the end, but the syllable in the middle sounded more like...
You rub your chin and ponder, but get interrupted by Dudu's nervous laughter.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: Ahaha, boss, your imagination is too wild. Of course she's saying "Parma." What else could she be saying?

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: Let's go see what clues we can find from the elm tree and chicken coop she was talking about...
She pulls your arm and walks out as she speaks, trying to change the subject. Seeing her pompous and guilty reaction, you get a pretty good sense of   what's going on.
After all the trouble just now, you're pretty sure that the delirious old lady has nothing to do with Parma, but you still let Dudu drag you along and continue the investigation.
First, it's a good chance to observe how people live in the Drifter Camp, and second, you want to see what tricks Dudu has up her sleeve.
You send the other team members back to the Bureau, and delve deeper into the Drifter Camp with Dudu on your own.

Dudu first climbs onto an old elm tree in front of the vegetable market and pretends to search around. As you expect, she finds nothing, then scampers away with the excuse of "searching the chicken coop."
While she's gone, you try to strike up conversations with the residents here. Seeing that you came with Dudu, they don't seem to be on guard against you.
Hi, excuse me, do you know Parma?
The blacksmith stops cleaning his furnace and looks at you, puzzled.

steps.speaker: Blacksmith
steps.content: Parma? You mean as in Parmesan cheese?
You're speechless for a moment.
You know... The one that the granny who lives in the southeast corner is always mumbling about...?
The blacksmith seems to have an epiphany and lets out a hearty laugh.

steps.speaker: Blacksmith
steps.content: Oh, so it's "Parma," is it? I could never tell what she was mumbling about. Haha, my ears are no match against you young folks'.

options: Do you know that lady well?

choices.text: Do you know that lady well?

steps.speaker: Blacksmith
steps.content: Oh, I know her all right. She was a well-known shrew in our Drifter Camp back in the day. Even the most vicious gangsters avoided her when they saw her. In a fight, she can curse with the strength of ten people, and yell at you so hard that you get a heart attack. It was terrifying!
This information catches you by surprise. Although you could tell from the old lady's face that she's not a kind and gentle character, you didn't expect her to have such a notorious reputation.
The blacksmith lets out a long sigh, then changes the subject.

steps.speaker: Blacksmith
steps.content: But ever since she got that tumor in her head a few years ago, she's completely lost it. Now she's dazed all day, and can't even take care of herself.

steps.speaker: Blacksmith
steps.content: So now, Dudu does all her cleaning and plumbing. She does all this hard work for free, but still has to endure that crazy woman's tantrums. It's really tough for Dudu.

options: Dudu would do things like that?!

choices.text: Dudu would do things like that?!

steps.content: You can't help but blurt out your doubt. The blacksmith looks at you long and hard.

steps.speaker: Blacksmith
steps.content: You must've met Dudu not long ago, so you still don't know her well, eh?

steps.speaker: Blacksmith
steps.content: The little tyke's got a lot of bad habits, that's for sure. She's cunning, greedy, annoying, a freeloader, full of bad ideas, and loves to fool others... But she's definitely not a bad or selfish person.

steps.speaker: Blacksmith
steps.content: Didn't that crazy woman's condition worsen over the past two days? Dudu must have been worried after hearing the news, so she hurried back.

steps.speaker: Blacksmith
steps.content: Although Dudu's an Outlander, we all know that she thinks of the Drifter Camp as her home and us as her family. She does all those chores voluntarily, and while she complains, she never stops her actions of care and love. Isn't that what family does?
Really...
The Dudu described by the blacksmith is so different from the Dudu you know. Then... which one is the real her?
As you lower your head to ponder, an energetic voice rings out.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: Boss! I'm back!

Dudu stands before you with messy hair and chicken feathers all over her body, as if afraid that others won't know where she went. You suppress your laugh as you help pick off the feathers and tidy her hair.
You already know the answer, but you still ask her as a formality.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: Sigh, what a bummer. I didn't find Parma. Just eggs.
Yet there's no sign of disappointment on her face. She weighs the eggs in her hands a few times, then slips them into her pocket.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: But it wasn't a wasted trip. I can get an extra meal when we go back.
The little boy who has been curiously listening to you chat stares at the scattered chicken feathers in fear, then shifts his shocked gaze to Dudu.
You suddenly remember that Dudu told you about a poor kid in the camp who got chased by a goose and became terrified of birds. This is probably him.

steps.speaker: Blacksmith's Son
steps.content: You got pecked, too, Dudu?
The little boy asks timidly, but Dudu flashes him a bright smile.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: How's that possible? This is from my epic battle with it.

steps.speaker: Blacksmith's Son
steps.content: Then did you win?

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: Do you even need to ask? Of course I won!

steps.speaker: Blacksmith's Son
steps.content: You're so cool, Dudu! How did you win?

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: Ta-da! My invincible suona! Whether it's a chicken, duck or goose, one song will scare 'em away!
Dudu proudly takes out her suona, and the little boy looks at her with adoring eyes.

steps.speaker: Blacksmith's Son
steps.content: Wow!

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: Want to hear it?

steps.speaker: Blacksmith's Son
steps.content: Yeah!

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: Then I'll play you a song...

steps.speaker: Blacksmith
steps.content: Stop! We don't want to be extorted again!
Just as Dudu raises her suona to play, the blacksmith stops her in annoyance. Dudu doesn't get angry. She simply puts away her suona and makes a face at the little boy.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: I'll stop, otherwise your dad will beat me. But I can teach you how to play the suona, so that you don't have to be scared of geese anymore.

steps.speaker: Blacksmith
steps.content: Shush! Stop fooling my kid! I'll really beat you if you don't leave!
The blacksmith starts shooing her away with the rag in his hand. Dudu sticks out her tongue at him, then drags you away.
She pulls you nimbly through the narrow alleys of the Drifter Camp. You gaze at the light and shadows cast upon her hair by the golden afternoon sun, feeling suddenly dazed.
In this moment, she's like a fairy who has strayed into the mortal world, forever lively, free, happy and unrestrained.
Next, you guys come to a vegetable stall.

steps.speaker: Vegetable Seller
steps.content: Parma? Never heard of it.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: Then can you tell my boss about the old lady who lives alone in the southeast corner?
She takes one look at Dudu and waves her hand impatiently.

steps.speaker: Vegetable Seller
steps.content: I don't care who's with you. Go go go. Don't get in the way of my business.
A grinning Dudu fishes out your wallet from your pocket and generously pulls out a couple of large bills for the seller.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: Keep the change, ma'am. A few random veggies will do.
Hey...
You reach out in alarm to stop Dudu, but the vegetable seller swiftly grabs the money and stuffs it into her pocket. She flashes you a fawning smile, reversing her attitude completely.

steps.speaker: Vegetable Seller
steps.content: Your boss wants to know about that old hag, right?

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: Yes!
You look at Dudu in exasperation, but she winks at you without any remorse, as if to say, "This is how we do things in the Drifter Camp."

steps.speaker: Vegetable Seller
steps.content: That piece of work, tsk tsk... Back when she was still clear-headed, she'd haggle with me for half an hour for a green onion or two. I was really scared of her.

steps.speaker: Vegetable Seller
steps.content: This must be her karma for being so cruel and callous when she was young. Now she can only die alone.
As she says these unkind words, she shoves a big bag of vegetables into your arms.

steps.speaker: Vegetable Seller
steps.content: That's all I know, boss. Thank you, come again.
However, when you turn to leave, you hear her telling her daughter to cook some extra food for the evening to give to the old lady.
Doesn't the vegetable seller despise the old lady?
You ask Dudu in confusion, but Dudu responds matter-of-factly.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: Yeah. Everyone in the Drifter Camp despises her. So?
Then why did she ask her daughter to give her food?
Dudu sighs.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: We can't just watch the old lady starve to death. She's childless and has no one to take care of her to begin with. Now that she's lost her mind, she can't do anything.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: That's why people like us have to step up and take the responsibility. The vegetable seller would bring her food regularly, while the blacksmith would go to her house every now and then to see if anything needs fixing. As for me, I just help with some cleaning and chores.
...That's why her home is so clean.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: To tell you the truth, no one likes this kind of thankless work. It's dirty, tiring and unpaid, and sometimes she yells at me for no reason. There are times when my temper flares up and I swear to quit, but then I feel sorry for her again when I see her staring blankly out the window and mumbling to herself.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: If even we don't take care of her, she'll really end up dead. After all, we're the only ones she can rely on.
Deep in thought, you pace through the narrow alleys of the Drifter Camp with a big bag of vegetables in your arms. The sun overhead has already set.
Although you didn't get any information about Parma today, it was by no means a fruitless trip.
The Drifter Camp you witnessed is completely different from what you had imagined. Even the jabbering girl beside you seems more vivid and adorable now.

The sincerity between the camp residents makes you feel unprecedentedly relaxed. Here, no one has to put on a facade or watch their backs. People can be their truest selves, and express their truest thoughts with the frankest words.
Everyone here is struggling for survival, but they still love life. They are doing their best to live every day.

They despise the old lady, yet voluntarily take care of her. One should not judge someone's nature by what they say, but by what they do. Their plebeian vulgarities cannot conceal their warm and kind hearts.
It's getting late. Let's head back to the Bureau.
Dudu looks at the vegetables in your arms, her eyes shifting about. You wonder what tricks she's come up with this time.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: Wait a minute! I know!

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: Let's go to one last place! Maybe we'll be able to find something!

The person you're visiting this time is the oldest man in the Drifter Camp. He has lived alone in a remote corner of the camp for many years. People say he's withdrawn and eccentric, and knows many things that others don't.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: Gramps, it's me, Dudu! Are you surprised?
The old man who answered the door snorts.

steps.speaker: Old Man
steps.content: What's there to be surprised about? Who else besides you would run around all over the place for no reason?

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: Sigh, I haven't seen you for so long. Don't you miss me at all? Look, I brought so much food for you.

As soon as you enter the house, Dudu grabs the vegetables from your hands and puts them on the dining table. After going through the plastic bag, the old man's face finally lightens up, and he nods towards you.

steps.speaker: Old Man
steps.content: I knew a little devil like you would have ulterior motives. Tell me, what do you want from me this time?

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: Hehe... Well, the thing is, my boss has a question for you.
As she says this, Dudu elbows you a few times, hinting for you to speak.
Do you know what is this "Parma" that the old lady from the southeast corner is always mumbling about?
You tiredly repeat this question that you've been asking over and over again all day, but this time, you get a different answer.
The old man looks at you, then at Dudu, then flashes a knowing expression.

steps.speaker: Old Man
steps.content: If you mean the lady with the brain tumor, then what she's saying is <color=#fb9259>"Palama"</color>, not "Parma."

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: What? Palama?!

Dudu cries out in surprise. This is the first time today that you see a look of genuine surprise on her face. You calmly press Dudu's arm to tell her not to get too excited. She quiets down and glances at you guiltily.
Ever since you left the old lady's house, you no longer hold any expectations about investigating Parma. Instead, this "Palama" that appeared out of the blue has piqued your interest.
What could Palama be? A type of homophony? A mysterious person? An important item? Or... a code name the common folk use for a certain event? Whatever it is, it's worth investigating.
Can you tell me more about this "Palama"?

steps.speaker: Old Man
steps.content: So many years have passed in the blink of an eye. I'm probably the only person here who still remembers Palama.
...Remembers? The strange wording makes you frown.

steps.speaker: Old Man
steps.content: There is an abandoned building about three or four hundred meters to the northwest of the Drifter Camp. Palama is inside.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: The abandoned building that was struck by lightning?
You know it?

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: Of course. It's one of the Drifter Camp's most infamous tragedies... One stormy night many years ago, roaring thunder shook the land, and there was so much lightning that the entire night sky was lit up. The Drifter Camp had never experienced anything like it.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: Suddenly, a lightning bolt struck the antenna on top of that building, instantly lighting up the whole structure in flames. The fire was so big that it burned for a whole day and night before it got finally put out. They say that many people didn't escape in time and burned to death inside.
The old man continues on from Dudu.

steps.speaker: Old Man
steps.content: Precisely. It became a notorious haunted building ever since. With dozens of wronged souls trapped inside, it'd be strange for it not to be haunted! Many young daredevils have gone to explore it in the middle of the night, but every single one of them ended up fleeing while peeing their pants.

steps.speaker: Old Man
steps.content: They say there's a female ghost dressed in white who wanders through the rooms, weeping and muttering incomprehensible words. Sometimes it's low-pitched sobs, other times it's hysterical screams and wails. It's really eerie.

steps.speaker: Old Man
steps.content: And Palama is inside that building.
After finishing his sentence, the old man shakes his head and goes into another room, leaving you and Dudu in the empty living room.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: Um... boss... about "Parma," I can explain...
Dudu breaks the silence first. She chuckles awkwardly as she cautiously tugs on your sleeve.
Enough. You think I didn't know that you made up the so-called "Parma intelligence"?

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: Y-you already knew? Then why did you come here with me?

You must have your reasons for wanting to return to the camp so urgently. Now I know it's because you wanted to see the old lady after learning about her worsening condition from the intelligence agent, right? If this is the reason, you could've told me from the start. I would've let you come back.
Dudu's eyes glimmer. She lowers her head in guilt.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: You guessed it, boss. I made up the story about "Parma" and tricked you into bringing me back here because I was worried about the old lady. But after seeing that she's fine, I wanted to see everyone in the camp who I haven't seen for a long time. I made you run around with me all day, and also spent a lot of your money ...

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: I shouldn't have done this... I'm sorry.
Then can you tell me the truth now? What is Palama, and what's the connection with that abandoned building?
To your surprise, Dudu shakes her head.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: I've asked many people in the Drifter Camp what "Pa-something-ma" was, but everyone thought it was just the old lady's delusions. In fact, today's the first time that I found out that she's actually saying "Palama."

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: As for what that word means and how it's connected to that building, I really don't have a clue... I'm telling the truth this time! You've got to believe me, boss!
Should we still go to that abandoned building, then?

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: Of course we should. The old lady entrusted me with arranging her funeral. I have to find out what is this "Palama" that she still yearns for despite losing her mind.
Dudu laughs.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: I can always ask Oak Casket to help realize her unfulfilled wishes after death, but if possible, I still want to clarify this matter when she's still alive.
You bid farewell to the old man and prepare to head northwest to the abandoned building. Before leaving, Dudu scoops out an arm-long green onion from the grocery bag and holds it in front of you.
You look at her incredulously.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: What if we run into danger? I have my suona with me, so I'm not afraid, but you don't have any handy weapons. Make do with this. Something is better than nothing.
As she says this, she swings the green onion a couple of times like a club. The water sprinkled on it by the vegetable seller splashes all over your face.
You wipe your face and look at the serious-faced Dudu in exasperation.
Even if those ghost stories, which are probably made up to scare people, are real, a green onion is totally useless as a weapon...
